subject: mandarin-chinese
summary: Mandarin cards are short, in English, and uncluttered; Chinese characters render correctly in the scheme and in the attached pages. Every card depends on its attached page (text, flyer, or picture grid), and the attachment is the right question each time, though it is the whole question page so sibling parts (a), (b) are visible on it. The main faults are schemes that do not match the shape of the question: 'name three' answered by one slash-joined line with a single tick, a three-part question whose answers are not labelled (i)-(iii), and a picture-matching question that cannot be attempted without opening the attachment. The orange underline stops mid-phrase on several cards.

issues.title: List answer collapsed into one slash-joined line
issues.detail: The question asks for three of four body parts for 3 marks. The scheme shows one tick box reading 'eyes / ears / hands / feet (paws)'. The student cannot tick the three they got and the app cannot suggest a mark out of 3.
issues.suggested_fix: Four separate tick items under 'Any 3 of these - 1 mark each'.

issues.title: Three sub-questions run together and answers not labelled
issues.detail: The stem 'Answer the following questions about the zoo tickets.' is printed twice (once as a small line, again at the start of the question), then (i), (ii), (iii) follow as one paragraph of eight lines on the phone. The scheme lists '8 yuan/kuai', '35 yuan/kuai / the family ticket', '60 yuan/kuai' with no (i)/(ii)/(iii) labels and no marks per item, and uses slashes for alternatives.
issues.suggested_fix: Show the stem once; put (i), (ii), (iii) on separate lines; label each scheme answer with its part and 2 marks; write '8 yuan (or kuai)'.

issues.title: Matching question cannot be read without the attachment
issues.detail: The card says only 'Match the following words and pictures by filling in the grid below' - there is no grid, no words and no pictures on the card. Everything is behind the attachment button, which is titled generically 'The material this question is about'. The scheme lists pairs as 'T恤 C', '裤子 D' with nothing between word and letter, and the letters only mean something with the picture page open.
issues.suggested_fix: Show a crop of the pictures and word grid directly in the question area; in the scheme write each pair as 'T恤 - C (T-shirt)' or show the completed grid from the scheme as an image.

issues.title: Orange underline cuts off mid-phrase
issues.detail: The underline covers 'According to the text, why do some of the young people like' and stops before 'to go to town squares'; on card 4 it covers 'Match the following words and pictures by filling' and stops; on card 3 it covers only 'Answer the following questions'.
issues.suggested_fix: Underline only the command word or phrase, on sensible boundaries, or remove it.

issues.title: Attached page shows sibling parts and a generic label
issues.detail: The attachment is the full first page of the question, so on card 1 parts (a) and (b) of Question 2 with their answer boxes are visible below the passage. The button is labelled 'READ QUESTION 2 / The material this question is about' rather than saying what it is (the passage, the flyer, the pictures). For cards 2, 3 and 5 only one page is attached and the visible top of it shows the heading and pictures or the first half of the flyer; the screenshot does not show whether the ticket prices or passage text needed for the answer are lower on that same page.
issues.suggested_fix: Crop the attachment to the passage or flyer box and label it 'Read the passage' / 'See the flyer'. Check that the single attached page contains all the text each question needs.

issues.title: No marks shown per scheme point
issues.detail: Card 5 is 4 marks with two points and card 2 is 4 marks with one sentence, but no marks are attached to the points, so the split is left to the student.
issues.suggested_fix: Show '2 marks each' where the scheme gives a split.

good_examples.why: Short question, two plain scheme steps, compact on the phone
Clear question and a one-sentence scheme answer that plainly answers it
